the platform shrinks behind glass, already becoming memory
fields unrolling like a letter written slowly, just for you
someone's seat still warm, their window still breathing fog
the space between stations where nothing is required of you
late afternoon light deciding which passenger to rest on
a town you almost lived in sliding past without knowing
the gentle tyranny of a journey with no decisions left
overhead luggage and the weight of everything left unsaid
rain on the window making the outside world impressionist
the particular quiet of strangers agreeing to be alone together
your reflection and the mountain sharing the same cold glass
ticket tucked in a pocket like a permission slip for elsewhere
the conductor's voice arriving from somewhere soft and far away
countryside repeating itself the way a good feeling does
two stops from home and already half-arriving in your mind
the small ceremony of folding a map no longer needed
morning mist held gently between one valley and the next
a vending coffee warming both hands and no particular thought
departure boards changing like slow advice from a patient friend
the lull of the rail joining one version of you to another
autumn through glass, the colour of almost but not quite
the unhurried arithmetic of distance and afternoon dissolving together
someone leaning their head against the window, practicing patience
returning to a place that held you once, still holding
